GRADE 2 · BEAN SPROUT / GROWTH

A bean becomes.

So much can happen before we see a leaf.

FOUR LITTLE WONDERS

Where shall we look?

Start with a question. Look for a little while. There is no hurry to know.

01What is waking up inside this little bean?↗02How does a root find its way when it cannot see?↗03What can a leaf do that a seed cannot?↗04How could we notice a change too slow to watch?↗

Grown-up beside you. A question is enough.

LOOK TOGETHER · 01

What is waking up inside this little bean?

Look inside the seed coat. What might those two pale halves be keeping safe?

A little explanation & something to try

A tiny plant is already inside. The bean holds food to help it begin.

Try together. Curl one hand like a seed. Slowly uncurl a finger for its first root.

LOOK TOGETHER · 02

How does a root find its way when it cannot see?

Follow the white root down. Now follow the little shoot up. What do you notice?

A little explanation & something to try

The root does not need eyes. It responds to gravity, which helps it grow down.

Try together. Trace the two directions in the air: root down, shoot up.

LOOK TOGETHER · 03

What can a leaf do that a seed cannot?

Find the three notes around the leaves. Where does each arrow lead?

A little explanation & something to try

Green leaves use light, water, and part of the air to make new food. The seed began with food stored inside.

Try together. Trace a path from the roots to a leaf. Then point to the light.

LOOK TOGETHER · 04

How could we notice a change too slow to watch?

Find the earlier mark and today's tip. What could a drawing help us remember?

A little explanation & something to try

We can compare notes from different days. Growth can happen too slowly for our eyes to catch it happening.

Try together. Hold a finger at the earlier mark. With your other hand, show the space up to today's tip.

KEEP THE SAME LITTLE WORLD

Let the pictures lead you on.

Read together. Measure a change. Give an idea your own words.

The quiet work of growing

A STORY TO OPEN TOGETHER

A bean becomes.

A little bean. A big beginning. Grown-up reads; little wonderer turns the page.

One little page at a time.

A beginning inside

Small, but not empty

Little Wonderer looks at the bean. “Is anything in there?” A tiny plant is tucked inside. Stored food will help it begin.

Point to the pale food stores.

Two ways to grow

Down and up

With water, air, and enough warmth, the bean starts to grow. A root comes out first. It responds to gravity and grows down. A shoot grows up.

Trace each path with a finger.

Leaves in the light

A new way to make food

Leaves open in the light. They use light, water, and carbon dioxide from the air to make food. The little plant can make more of what it needs.

Follow the three orange notes.

A change worth keeping

Too slow to see?

“It looks the same,” says Little Wonderer. Big Wonderer opens their notebook. An earlier mark is lower than today's tip. Their notes help them see a change.

What did the notebook help them remember?

A beginning inside

Look back at the beginning

“Did the bean need leaves to begin?” they wonder. Look inside it again. The tiny plant had stored food before it had open leaves.

What in the picture helps explain your answer?

A change worth keeping

A question to keep

They sit together by the window. Growing takes time. “What might change next?” asks Big Wonderer. Little Wonderer has a new question to draw.

Tell each other one thing you still wonder.

Measure a change →

MEASURE A CHANGE · ABOUT 15 MIN

How much did it grow?

Look at the earlier mark in the picture. Now use these pretend notebook measurements, all taken from the soil to the plant's tip.

Pretend notebook · height above soil
Day4812
Height8 cm14 cm23 cm

Would every real bean grow this much? No. These numbers are invented for our math story; real growth varies.

COMPARE TWO HEIGHTS

On Day 4 it was 8 cm tall. On Day 8 it was 14 cm. How much taller?

Start at 8. Hop 2 to 10, then 4 to 14.

IMAGINE A LITTLE MORE

On Day 12 it was 23 cm. In our number story, it later grows 9 cm more. How tall then?

A small hint

Add 7 to reach 30. How much of the 9 is left?

COUNT THE DAYS BETWEEN

How many days pass from Day 4 to Day 12? Count the spaces between days.

A small hint

Day 4 to Day 5 is one day. Count forward from there.

Use paper, draw a hop, or tell someone your thinking.

A note for your grown-up

About 15 min: 3 to choose and talk, 4 to draw, 6 to write 1–3 sentences, 2 to read back. Accept invented spelling, speech, or dictation. One careful idea is enough.

Small discoveries. Time together.

For grown-ups & print downloads

Wonder first; explanations can wait. Images are simplified, enlarged cutaways, not photographs or a timed growth record. Roots respond to gravity and other conditions; they do not think or see. Seeds need water, oxygen, and suitable warmth; the bean begins with stored food. Green leaves later make food. No real planting is required. Work together and stop when you have had enough.

About 15 min: look at the scenes, read the six short beats, then talk. Ask what changed in your child's idea. Point, speak, or pause; no independent reading required.
